questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 4 + 4 + 4?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 4 + 4 + 4 ?
questions.explain: Count the 4s: there are 3 of them, so this is 3 groups of 4, which is 3 × 4 = 12. Counting one group too few gives 2 × 4, which is 4 too little, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 4 × 4 or 2 × 3. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stem: Xin Yi works out 1171 + 7468 in columns. One column makes 13, so she writes 3 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is the 3 she writes there worth?
questions.stemText: Xin Yi works out 1171 + 7468 in columns. One column makes 13, so she writes 3 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is the 3 she writes there worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 13 is the tens column: 7 + 6 = 13, and no other column reaches ten. 13 tens is 1 hundred and 3 tens, so the 3 stays in the tens column - worth 30 - and the small 1 goes above the hundreds column - worth 100. The 3 is worth 30. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.stemText: Mei Ling works out 23 + 24 in her head. She makes 30 first. 23 + 24 = 30 + ?
questions.explain: To get from 23 up to 30 you need 7, so 7 is moved across from the 24. That leaves 24 − 7 = 17, and 30 + 17 = 47. questions.stemText: Which of these fractions is between 2/12 and 3/4?
questions.explain: Step 1: the two ends are not written in the same size of piece, so cut 34 into 12ths first: 3 × 3 = 9 and 4 × 3 = 12, so 34 is the same amount as 912. Step 2: now every fraction is in 12ths, so just count the tops - the answer has to be more than 2 of them and fewer than 9. questions.stemText: Wei Jie works out 1.47 + 1.9 . Wei Jie writes the 9 underneath the 7 and gets 1.66 . What is the correct answer?

questions.stem: A rectangular banner is 17 cm long and 10 cm wide. A notch 4 cm wide and 2 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 3 cm of edge before the notch and 10 cm after it, and the banner is still 8 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.stemText: A rectangular banner is 17 cm long and 10 cm wide. A notch 4 cm wide and 2 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 3 cm of edge before the notch and 10 cm after it, and the banner is still 8 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.explain: Walk the eight sides: 3 + 2 + 4 + 2 + 10 + 10 + 17 + 10 = 58 cm. Careful: this notch is in the middle of a side, not at a corner. The 4 cm taken out of the top edge is replaced by the 4 cm along the bottom of the notch, so that part of the walk is unchanged. But the two sides of the notch, 2 cm down and 2 cm back up, are brand new. Perimeter = 2 × (17 + 10) + 2 × 2 = 58 cm. A corner cut leaves the perimeter alone; a middle notch makes it longer.
